Plot the recovery of true effects in simulated data

Source: R/plot-recovery.R
plot_recovery.Rd

For simulated data, where the true effects are known, plot_recovery() compares a fit with the truth. It shows the posterior intervals of the sites together with the true effects, the proportion of intervals that contain the true effect at each level, or the posterior means against the true effects.

Usage

plot_recovery(
  x,
  truth,
  type = c("intervals", "calibration", "scatter"),
  level = 0.9,
  n = 150,
  seed = NULL,
  scale = 1,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A bef_fit object created by bayes_efron_fit().

truth

Numeric vector of true effects, one per site, in the same order as the sites in the data.

type

Type of plot: "intervals" (the default), "calibration" or "scatter". See Details.

level

Posterior probability of the intervals, a number between 0 and 1. Only used with type = "intervals".

n

Maximum number of sites shown with type = "intervals", an integer of at least 1.

seed

Integer seed for the random choice of sites. If NULL (the default), the current state of R's random number generator is used.

scale

Positive number by which the effects are multiplied in the plot, e.g., 100 to show differences of proportions in percentage points. Not used with type = "calibration".

...

These dots are for future extensions and must be empty.

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

type selects one of three plots.

  • "intervals" shows the posterior interval and the true effect of each site, with the sites ordered by posterior mean, and marks the sites where the true effect lies outside the interval. If there are more than n sites, n of them are chosen at random; specify seed to make the choice reproducible.

  • "calibration" shows, for levels from 5% to 95%, the proportion of all sites with the true effect inside the posterior interval of that level. The intervals are the ones that confint.bef_fit_re() returns. They are computed from the posterior distribution of each effect and not from a normal approximation, which would give wrong intervals for sites with a bimodal posterior distribution.

  • "scatter" shows the posterior means against the true effects. The caption gives the root mean squared error of the posterior means and of the estimates.

The proportions in these plots describe one data set. They are not the coverage of the intervals, which is the average of such a proportion over repeated data sets. The intervals of all sites depend on the same estimate of \(g\), so they tend to miss together, and the proportion in one data set varies around the nominal level more than it would for independent sites.

See also

site_summary(), confint.bef_fit_re(), vignette("twin-towers")

Examples

truth <- twin_towers$theta_true
plot_recovery(twin_towers_fit, truth, seed = 1)

plot_recovery(twin_towers_fit, truth, type = "calibration")

plot_recovery(twin_towers_fit, truth, type = "scatter")
